name: Subsea power and umbilical systems
principle: Subsea electrical systems take power from a platform or shore through a power umbilical — cable plus steel tubes for hydraulic signals — to subsea distribution units, transformers, variable speed drives and motors on the seabed. Moves toward higher voltage and longer step-outs have already delivered megawatt-class subsea compression, where the whole drive train sits on the seabed without an topsides compressor. Reliability engineering, connector technology and dynamic cable design for floating hosts dominate the design space.

process_steps.name: Topside or onshore supply conditioned and stepped for export
Power umbilical and static/dynamic cable delivered to the seabed
Subsea distribution and step-down feed seabed loads
Motors, drives and valve actuators run on the seabed

limitations: wet-mate connectors and repairability set availability limits; interventions are vessel-based and costly
dynamic cables on floating production see fatigue that dominates their design
advantages: eliminates long risers and topsides compression weight and space
enables long-distance tiebacks and seabed boosting where topsides power would be prohibitive
